cases.name: Gayle Ann Botelho
cases.narrative:
In 2000, her skeletal remains were found buried in a backyard on June Street. 

Gayle Botelho and her boyfriend owed Tavares money for cocaine. “What he said was that he had more cocaine, that he had a deal, essentially, for her,” McCauley said. “He was going to front her some cocaine so they could sell it so they could raise money to pay him back.” Tavares laid out a line of cocaine in the bedroom of his home for Botelho, McCauley said. As she bent to inhale it, Tavares pulled a gun that he tried, unsuccessfully, to fire, McCauley said. “She was grabbed by the hair, pulled to the body and stabbed repeatedly,” McCauley said. “He described how thick the blood was, the smell of the blood. He described the noises she made, how she attempted to breathe as blood filled her mouth.” Tavares dropped Botelho’s body off a second floor porch and buried her under a tree in his backyard, McCauley told the jurors. She was not found until Tavares lead police there in 2000. At the time, prosecutors say, Tavares said he was only a witness to the killing."

“In 2000, he came up with a plan,” McCauley said. “His plan was to shave off time from his sentence by using the murder of Gayle Botelho.”

cases.name: Jessenia I. "Jessie" Simmons Montanez
cases.about:
Her Facebook said she studied at University of Puerto Rico, Rio Piedras Campus and was from Charlotte Amalie, U.S. Virgin Islands. It was reported Those who knew Simmons remember her as a caring, kind and loving person who always had a smile on her face and loved life. The Providence Hispanic Softball League Alliance and the Rosario Softball League, which Simmons was actively a part of, dedicated their tournament to her and forever retired her number 77 to make sure that she will never be forgotten.

A friend of Jessenia told us that she was a gem of a person and to know her was to love her.

“Jessie was a caring, kind and loving person. She always had a smile on her face every single time you saw her and was always so excited about life, she loved God and her kids like no other. She was so positive about life even when she was going through tough times.”
cases.narrative: First responders arrived on scene and found her already deceased in one of the car wash bays after being stabbed then shot.
